With reference to Mughal India, what is/are the diﬀ erence/diﬀ erences between Jagirdar and Zamindar? 1. Jagirdars were holders of land assignments in lieu of judicial and police duties, whereas Zamindars were holders of revenue rights without obligation to perform any duty other than revenue collection. 2. Land assignments to Jagirdars were hereditary had revenue rights of Zamindars were not hereditary. Select the correct answer using code given below : (a) 1 only (b) 2 only (c) Both 1 and 2 (d) Neither 1 nor 2 I.A.S. (Pre) 2019 Ans. (d) During Akbar's period, all the territory was broadly divided into two : Khalisa & Jagir. The revenue from the ﬁ rst went to imperial treasure & that from jagir was assigned to jagirdars in lieu of their salary in cash (raqd) according to their rank. Right to collect revenue was to utilize the same for their salary & to meet their military obligation. The judicial & police functions were performed locally by Zamindars. An important feature of the Jagir System was shifting of jagir-holders frame one jagir to another for administrative reasons. This system of transfers checked the jagirdars from developing local roots. Thus, jagirs were transferable & could be seized too. Zamindars, on the other hand, were hereditary. The Zamindars were present in practically every part of the Mughal Empire & held the most signiﬁ cant position in the agrarian structure of Mughal India. The word Zamindar is derived from two Persian words -Zamin (land) & dar (holder). 29. Which of the following Mughal period canals, was constructed by restoring the Rajabwah of Firuz Shah? In the time of Akbar, ﬁ rst Shihabuddin Khan & later Nuruddin Muhamad tar reconstructed the canal. During the time of Akbar, Governer of Delhi, Sihabuddin Khan, repaired the canal for irrigation purposes & changed its name to Shahab Canal. Music and Paintings of Mughal Period *War scenes, birds, animals and sceneries were illustrated in Mughal paintings. Humayun started the Mughal style of painting. He met two distinguished painters, Khwaja Abdus Samad and Mir Sayyid, during the years of his exile in Persia and Afghanistan. From these artists Humayun and his son Akbar learned lessons in drawing and painting. *Akbar got a number of texts painted. The ﬁ rst one was ‘Dastan-e-Amir Hamza’. Almost 50 painters took part in its preparation, ﬁ rst under the supervision of Sayyid Ali and later, under Abdu Samad. There were about 1400 paintings in it. This book mentioned the heroic work of the Persian hero, Amir Hamza (uncle of Muhammad Sahib). *The art of Mughal painting reached great heights during Jahangir’s reign. Jahangir was a highly skilled connoisseur of painting. Abul Hassan (the title of Nadir-Ud-Zama), Ustad Mansur (Nadir-ul-Asr), Faruq Begh, Bishan Das, Aqa Riza, Muhammad Nadir, Muhammad Murad Manohar, Madhav, Govardhan, etc were the main artists of Jahangir's court. Abul Hassan made a painting of Jahangir‘s coronation. This painting is inscribed in the Jahangir’s autobiography ‘Tujuk-e-Jahangiri’ on the main page. Thus, Jahangir’s period was called ‘Golden Age of Mughal Paintings'. *‘Pahari School’, ’Rajput School’, ‘Mughal School’ and ‘Kangra School’ are diﬀ erent styles of medieval painting. *Aurangzeb banned the music as he found it as anti-Islamic, but during the same period, maximum books on Indian classical music were written in the Persian language. Despite being anti-music. Aurangzeb was a skilled instrumentalist who used to play the Indian instrument called ‘Veena'. *‘Todi’ Raga is used to sing early in the morning. It was sung by Bhatos and Charans in the emperor’s court. *During the reign of Akbar, Tansen and Swami Haridas were prominent Dhrupad singers. Tansen was a famous musician of Akbar‘s court. Tansen‘s original name was Ramtanu Pandey. Indian History General Studies B–299 He was one of the Akbar’s Navratanas. Before coming to the court of Akbar, Tansen was in the court of King Ramchandra of Rewa from where Akbar summoned him to his court and gave a very high post. *Akbar had given Tansen the title of ‘Kanthabharnvanivilas’. *Vilas Khan was the chief musician of Jahangir’s court. The prominent singers of the court of Shah Jahan were Jagannath, Ramdas, Sukhsen, Sursen, Lal Khan, Durrang Khan, etc. Khyal singing became popular in the time of Muhammad Shah ‘Rangila’. *The Kishangarh style of Rajasthan is known throughout India for its depiction of courtesan paintings. Raja Sawant Singh was the real inspiration behind the famous Kishangarh School of Painting. The main artists of this style were Amirchand, Chhotu, Bhawanidas, Nihalchand, Sitaram etc. *The famous portrait of ‘Bani-Thani’ which is in Kishangarh style was made by Nihalchand. 1.
